clue.text: She's in no. 10 best-seller by King

definitions.meaning: ... Symonds (now Johnson) lived at 10 Downing Street as the Prime Minister's partner in 2020
Stephen King's first published novel, a horror hit about a telekinetic schoolgirl

explanation.surface: A pointer to a woman living at Downing Street, then a bestselling novel by a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks royal but is Stephen King the novelist; No 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's official home.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are one first name: the Prime Minister's partner of the day and the title of Stephen King's debut novel.

clue.text: Men biting animated dog

indicators.note: the animation letters close their jaws around the soldiers, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: CGI, computer-generated imagery, is how animated films are made
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A cartoon dog with a habit of biting men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biting' is the containment signal: the soldiers go inside the animation letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh breed of short-legged herding dog, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Run dry? Reject all suspect condiment

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not to be trusted, so these letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A kitchen order: if the sauce runs dry, throw out anything doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' shuffles the fifteen letters of RUN DRY REJECT ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fruit preserve served as an accompaniment to roast lamb, so it is a classic table sauce.

clue.text: Sick husband, upper-class, chopping in half Jose's pet

parts.note: sick means ill
U denotes upper-class, as in U and non-U speech

indicators.note: chopping the surname in half keeps only its first four letters

parts.note: Jose Mourinho, the Portuguese football manager

explanation.surface: A sick, posh husband takes an axe to Jose's pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal but means a sulk, fitting for the famously moody Mourinho; 'chopping in half' keeps MOUR from his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet in the old sense is a fit of sulking or peevishness, a bad mood.

clue.text: Celebrity Madrid coach suffering 1-0 reversal during first half

indicators.note: the coach's name suffers a change in its first half: the 1 (letter I) is turned into a 0 (letter O)

parts.note: Diego Simeone, long-time coach of Atlético Madrid

explanation.surface: A famous Madrid football manager goes a goal down before half-time.
explanation.walkthrough: The football score is the device: read 1 as I and 0 as O, and swap one for the other in the first half of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is a person of note, as in 'she thinks she's really somebody'.

clue.text: Tramps removing hospital instruments

indicators.note: removing says the hospital letter is taken away from the vagrants

parts.note: hoboes are American tramps
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Vagrants are cleared out of a hospital's equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes H from HOBOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-reed woodwind pieces played in orchestras are musical instruments.

clue.text: Freedom! Fishermen can net flounders!

definitions.note: a noun; freedom here is the right to vote or liberation

indicators.note: to flounder is to struggle about clumsily, so the letters thrash into a new order

explanation.surface: A cry of liberty for fishermen now allowed to catch flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flounders' looks like the fish being netted but is the anagram signal for FISHERMEN CAN NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given the vote, or released from slavery, is a grant of liberty or rights.

clue.text: Being from Japan, resent hopping about naked

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the stripped letters are read backwards
naked words are stripped of their outer covering, their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Japanese person, resentful at being made to hop around in the nude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopping about' reads as one phrase, but 'naked' strips the outer letters of both words and 'about' then turns the whole string round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippon is the Japanese name for Japan, so this adjective describes a native of that country.

clue.text: Cook up good puzzle

definitions.note: a verb: to cook on a flat iron plate

parts.note: a riddle is a puzzle

explanation.surface: An instruction to concoct a decent puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook up' suggests inventing something, but here it is literal frying.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook food on a heavy flat iron plate, as with pancakes or bacon.

clue.text: Stupid mistakes almost make one turn against parcel firm

indicators.note: almost means the phrase stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: to go off someone or something is to be put off it, to turn against it
UPS, United Parcel Service, the delivery company

explanation.surface: Blunders nearly cause a customer to fall out with a courier firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final F of GO OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal American slang for blunders or botches, close to slip-ups.

clue.text: Wine from Bordeaux finishes the Spanish actor

parts.note: vin is French for wine
dies means comes to an end, finishes
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: French wine polishes off a Spanish film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Star of the Fast and Furious films, an American screen performer.

clue.text: Africans buy UK IKEA retro covers

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the concealed letters are read in reverse
the words cover the letters, holding them within

explanation.surface: Africans shopping for backward-looking furniture covers in a British IKEA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' hides UYUKIK in 'buY UK IKea'; 'retro' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Kenya's largest ethnic group are a people of East Africa.

clue.text: Anne is so excited — on heat!

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Anne is getting rather worked up, apparently in a state of arousal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges ANNE IS SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A female animal ready to mate is said to be in that state, like a fruit available at its best time.

clue.text: In the beginning, second wave of really dangerous, terrible floods came, threatening suspension

indicators.note: in the beginning points to the opening letter of each of the next five words
terrible means dreadful, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding account of a second dangerous wave of deluges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the beginning' takes the first letters of 'second wave of really dangerous'; 'terrible' shuffles FLOODS CAME.
explanation.definitionFit: The courtier Damocles feasted under a blade hung by a single hair, an image of ever-present peril dangling overhead.

clue.text: You and I get up. Oman's boring, boring.

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: the first boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to arise is to get up
OM is the international code for Oman

explanation.surface: A grumpy traveller finds Oman dull from the moment of waking.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word has two jobs: the first 'boring' drills OM into ARISE, the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome and tedious is dull or uninteresting.

clue.text: Timid wren flying when it's really cold

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters flit about into a new order

explanation.surface: A shy little bird takes flight in the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges TIMID WREN.
explanation.definitionFit: The depth of winter, around the solstice, is the season of the harshest chill.

clue.text: Newspaper items which explain The Hulk's furrowed brow?

definitions.meaning: large-type titles across the top of a front page
Bruce Banner is the Hulk's human alter ego, and a furrowed brow has lines on the head

explanation.surface: Front-page splashes that account for the green giant's frown.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as BANNER (the Hulk's real name) + HEAD + LINES (wrinkles).
explanation.definitionFit: Big bold titles running across a newspaper's front page are the main stories' headings.

clue.text: Bond's boss played by Dench holds key — not one to underestimate!

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond films

indicators.note: holds says the remaining letters wrap around the musical key
not one means a letter for one, I, is dropped

parts.note: the role is played by the actor, so M is Judi Dench
the actress's first name, here spelt with an E
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: M, as played by Judi Dench, picks up a key and warns against underrating her.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse needs JUDIE, but the actress is Judi; the blog notes the setter admitted the slip. 'not one' drops one I, and 'holds' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To misjudge someone is to get their measure wrong, for instance by rating them too low.

clue.text: Intimidate crime writer, blowing kiss

indicators.note: blowing a kiss sends it away, so the kiss letter leaves the name

parts.note: Colin Dexter, author of the Inspector Morse novels
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A crime novelist blows a kiss to frighten someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing' removes X from DEXTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone off acting through fear is to scare or discourage them.

clue.text: Current Russian secret police supremo somewhere in Western Europe

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
Lavrentiy Beria, Stalin's head of the NKVD

explanation.surface: A sinister Soviet police chief is lurking in a Western country right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' but is the physics symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula of Spain and Portugal is a region in the west of the continent.

clue.text: Suggest Knut's pally every now and again

parts.note: Knut is the setter, so Knut's (Knut is) is I'm from his own mouth

indicators.note: every now and again picks only some of the letters, every other one

explanation.surface: A hint that the setter is rather chummy from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by name, so 'Knut's' is I'M; 'every now and again' takes P, L, Y from PALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without stating it is to suggest or insinuate.

clue.text: Gather senior officer is no longer with us

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
the late person is dead, no longer with us

explanation.surface: An assembly is told the colonel has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect pages or information together and put them in order is to assemble them.

clue.text: Have a go at short-term worker engaged by US telecom giant

indicators.note: a worker engaged by a firm is taken on inside it

parts.note: AT&T, the American telephone company
a temp is a temporary worker

explanation.surface: A temporary worker hired by a big American phone company tries their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords drop the ampersand from the company's name; 'engaged by' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To try one's hand at a task is to make a try at it.

clue.text: Frank, Roy, Wendy going west touring an eastern state

indicators.note: going west says the hidden letters are read backwards
touring says the letters travel around inside the three names, held within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Three friends heading west on a road trip around an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'touring' into the definition, which left the hidden word unsignalled; 'touring' is the hiding signal and the definition is 'an eastern state'. 'going west' reverses KROYWEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Empire State lies on the Atlantic seaboard of the USA.

clue.text: Sandy is so courageous

definitions.meaning: full of grit or sand particles

explanation.surface: Sandy is apparently a brave person.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is both coarse sand and dogged pluck, so the adjective covers both sandy texture and brave resolve.
